questions.q: According to the 1991 Census, the highest percentage of population in India is to be found in the age group of: [1995]
questions.e: According to the 1991 Census, the highest percentage of the Indian population was found in the 5-14 years age group.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs are correctly matched? [1995] 1️⃣ Increase in-Monetary expansion 2️⃣ Low import growth rate in India-Recession in Indian industry 3️⃣ Euro-issues-Shares held by Indian companies in European countries 4️⃣ Portfolio investment Foreign institutional investors.
questions.e: Euro issues include ADRs and GDRs, which are instruments for Indian companies to raise foreign currency resources from foreign investors, not shares held by Indian companies in Europe.

questions.q: Which one of the following is true regarding the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY)? [1995]
o: The target group of JRY are the urban poor living below the poverty line
Under the scheme 30% of the employment generated is reserved for women
It was launched during the Prime Ministership of Indira Gandhi
It aims at creating one million jobs annually
questions.e: JRY was targeted at the rural poor, with 30% of employment opportunities reserved for women in rural areas.

questions.q: The Narasimham Committee for financial sector Reforms has suggested reduction in [1995]
o: SLR and Financing to capital goods sector
CRR, Priority Sector Financing and Financing to capital goods sector
SLR, CRR and Priority Sector Financing
questions.e: The Narasimham Committee (1991) suggested reducing SLR and CRR, and cutting priority sector financing from 40% to 10%.

questions.q: Corporation tax: [1995]
o: is levied and appropriated by the States
is levied by the Union and belongs to it exclusively
is levied by the Union and collected and appropriated by the States
is levied by the Union and shared by the Union and the States
questions.e: Corporation tax is a direct tax levied, collected, and appropriated exclusively by the Central Government; no part is assigned to states.

questions.q: One of the reasons for India's occupational structure remaining more or less the same over the years has been that: [1995]
o: ceiling on land holdings have enabled more people to own land and hence their preference to stay with agriculture
investment pattern has been directed towards capital intensive industries
productivity in agriculture has been high enough to induce people to stay with agricultural
people are largely unaware of the significance of transition from agriculture to industry for economic development
questions.e: A primary reason for the stagnant occupational structure is that investment patterns historically favored capital-intensive industries rather than labor-intensive ones.

questions.q: The main reason for low growth rate in India, inspite of high rate of savings and capital formation is: [1995]
questions.e: A high capital-output ratio means more capital is required to produce one unit of output, indicating lower efficiency of capital.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct regarding stabilization and structural adjustment as two components of the new economic policy adopted in India? [1996]
o: Stabilization is a gradual, multi-step process while structural adjustment is a quick adaptation process
Stabilization and structural adjustment are very similar and complimentary policies. It is difficult to separate one from the other
Structural adjustment is a gradual multi-step process, while stabilization is a quick adaptation process
Stabilization mainly deals with a set of policies which are to be implemented by the Central government while structural adjacent is to be set it motion by the State governments
questions.e: In the 1991 New Economic Policy, stabilization is a short-term quick adaptation process, while structural adjustment is a long-term gradual process.

questions.q: One of the important goals of the economic liberalisation policy is to achieve full convertibility of the Indian rupee. This is being advocated because: [1996]
o: it will help India secure loans from the world financial markets at attractive terms
it will attract more foreign capital inflow in India
convertibility of the rupee will stabilize its exchange value against major currencies of the world
it will help to promote exports
questions.e: Full convertibility allows international investors to buy and sell Indian assets at will, which is expected to facilitate growth and higher foreign investment.

questions.q: Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R): Assertion (A): Though India's national income has gone up several fold since 1947, there has been no marked improvement in the per capita income level. Reason (R): Sizeable proportion of the population of India is still living below the poverty line. [1996]
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.e: While both statements are factually true, the existence of poverty is not the direct causal reason for the lack of improvement in per capita income compared to total national income growth.

questions.q: A redistribution of income in a country can be best brought about through: [1996]
o: progressive taxation combined with regressive expenditure
progressive taxation combined with progressive expenditure
regressive taxation combined with regressive expenditure
regressive taxation combined with progressive expenditure
questions.e: Progressive taxation (higher rates for higher income) combined with regressive expenditure (spending more on the poor) effectively redistributes income.

questions.q: As per the 1991 Census, the average size of households in terms of number of persons per household in respect of the given states follows the sequence (highest first, lowest last): [1996]
o: Gujarat, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal
Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Gujarat, Kerala
Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu
Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala
questions.e: Based on 1991 census data, the household size sequence from highest to lowest was Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Gujarat, and Kerala.

questions.q: Human Development Index comprises literacy rates, life expectancy at birth and: [1997]
o: Gross Domestic Product per head at real purchasing power
National Income per head in US dollars
Gross National Product per head in the US dollars
Gross National Product in US dollars
questions.e: The HDI, first calculated in 1990, measures life expectancy, literacy, and adjusted real income (standard of living).

questions.q: In India, inflation is measured by the: [1997]
o: Consumers Price Index for agricultural workers
Consumers Price Index for urban non-manual workers
questions.e: Historically, the WPI was the primary measure for inflation in India, covering a representative basket of wholesale goods.

questions.q: Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The emergence of economic globalism does not imply the decline of socialist ideology. Reason (R): The ideology of socialism believes in Universalism and globalism. [1997]
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.e: Socialism believes in universal application of principles; therefore, global movement of goods/services does not inherently contradict socialist universalism.

questions.q: National Income is: [1997]
o: Net Domestic Product at market price
Net National Product at market price
Net Domestic Product at factor cost
Net National Product at factor cost
questions.e: National Income is defined as the NNP at factor cost, representing the total income of all factors of production.

questions.q: The Minimum Alternative Tax (MAT) was introduced in the Budget of the Government of India for the year: [1997]
questions.e: MAT was introduced in 1996-97 to ensure companies with book profits pay a minimum tax even if their taxable income is zero under normal rules.

questions.q: Match List-I (Committee) with List-II (Chaired by): A. Disinvestment of shares in PSEs - B. Industrial Sickness - C. Tax Reforms - D. Reforms in Insurance Sector. [1997]
questions.e: The match is: Disinvestment (C. Rangarajan), Industrial Sickness (Omkar Goswami), Tax Reforms (Rajah Chelliah), and Insurance (R.N. Malhotra).

questions.q: What is the correct sequence of the descending order of the following States in respect of female literacy rates as per the 2001 census? 1️⃣ Mizoram 2️⃣ Kerala 3️⃣ Goa 4️⃣ Nagaland. [1997]
questions.e: As per 2001 census: Kerala (87.7%), Mizoram (86.7%), Goa (76.5%), and Nagaland (61.5%).

questions.q: The Capital Account Convertibility of the Indian Rupee implies: [1998]
o: that the Indian Rupee can be exchanged for any major currency for the purpose of trade in goods and services
that the Indian Rupee can be exchanged for any major currency for the purpose of trade in goods and services
that the Indian Rupee can be exchanged by the authorised dealers for travel
questions.e: Capital account convertibility means the free conversion of cross-border capital flows for trading financial assets.

questions.q: A consumer is said to be in equilibrium, if: [1998]
o: he is able to locate new sources of income
he is able to live in full comforts with a given level of income
he can fulfil his needs without consumption of certain items
he is able to fulfil his need with a given level of income
questions.e: Equilibrium is reached when a consumer cannot change their condition to improve satisfaction given their income and prices.

questions.q: The supply-side economics lays greater emphasis on the point of view of: [1998]
questions.e: Supply-side economics argues that economic growth is created by lowering barriers for people to produce goods and services.

questions.q: Human Poverty Index was introduced in the Human Development Report of the year: [1998]
questions.e: The HPI was first reported in 1997 by the UN to complement the Human Development Index.

questions.q: The current Price Index (base 1960) is nearly 330. This means that the price of: [1998]
o: the price of certain selected items have gone upto 3.3 times
gold price has gone up 3.3 times
weighted mean of price of certain items has increased 3.3 times
all items cost 3.3 times more than what they did in 1960
questions.e: A price index of 330 means the weighted average price of the items in the basket has increased 3.3 times relative to the base year.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Devaluation of a currency may promote export. Reason (R): Price of the country's products in the international market may fall due to devaluation. [1999]
o: A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.e: Devaluation makes a country's goods cheaper for foreigners, increasing their competitiveness and promoting exports.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Fiscal deficit is greater than budgetary deficit. Reason (R): Fiscal deficit is the borrowing from the Reserve Bank of India plus other liabilities of the Government to meet its expenditure. [1999]
o: Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
questions.e: Fiscal deficit includes the budget deficit plus all other borrowings and liabilities, making it inherently larger.

questions.q: Persons below the poverty line in India are classified as such based whether: [1999]
o: their daily wages fall below the prescribed minimum wages
they are entitled to a minimum prescribed food basket
they belong to agricultural labourer household and the scheduled caste/tribe social group
they get work for a prescribed minimum number of days in a year
questions.e: Historically, India defined the poverty line based on the expenditure required to buy a food basket worth 2,400 calories in rural areas and 2,100 in urban areas.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements regarding the levying, collecting and distribution of Income Tax is correct? [1999]
o: The Union levies, collects and distributes the proceeds of income tax between itself and the states
The Union levies and collects the tax but all the proceeds are distributed among the states
The Union levies, collects and keeps all the proceeds of income tax to itself
Only the surcharge levied on income tax is shared between the Union and the states
questions.e: Income tax is levied and collected by the Union government and the proceeds are distributed between the Union and the states.

questions.q: Among which one of the following sets of social/religious groups is the extent of poverty the highest, as per Government statistics for the nineties? [1999]
o: Tribals in Bihar, Orissa, M.P. and Maharashtra
Scheduled Caste in Punjab, Western UP, Northern Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu
Christians in Gujarat, Maharashtra and Assam
Muslims in Kerala, Gujarat and A.P.
questions.e: In the 1990s, the incidence of poverty was statistically highest among the tribal populations of Bihar, Orissa, M.P., and Maharashtra.

questions.q: The first Indian State to have its Human Development Report prepared and released by Amartya Kumar Sen in Delhi is: [1999]
questions.e: Madhya Pradesh was the first state to release an HDR in 1995 under the guidance of Prof. Amartya Sen.

questions.q: In an open economy, the national income (Y) of the economy is: (C, I, G, X, M stand for Consumption, Investment, Govt. Expenditure, total exports and total imports respectively.) [2000]
questions.e: The national income accounting identity for an open economy is $Y=C+I+G+(X-M)$.

questions.q: Match List I with List II (Business Cycle): A. Boom - B. Recession - C. Depression - D. Recovery. [2001]
questions.e: Boom is high activity; Recession is falling activity; Depression is severe prolonged downturn; Recovery is the rise following a recession.

questions.q: Indian Human Development Report does not give for each sample village: [2000]
questions.e: The HDR calculates indices for development, gender disparity, and poverty, but not specifically an unemployment index for each sample village.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the megacities of India: 1️⃣ Population of each megacity is more than 5 million 2️⃣ All the megacities are important sea ports 3️⃣ Megacities are either national or state capitals. [2000]
questions.e: While megacities have over 5 million people, some (like Delhi) are landlocked and not sea ports.

questions.q: Which one of the following ports of India handles the highest tonnage of import cargo? [2000]
questions.e: Kandla Port handled the highest volume of traffic in the period specified in the source.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is false? [2000]
o: All countries other than India have over 80% literacy
The life expectancy at birth in India is almost the same as that of Indonesia
Malaysia and Korea have life expectancy higher than all other countries
Higher the adult literacy lower is the infant mortality
questions.e: According to the table provided, India's life expectancy was 62.4 while Indonesia's was 64.

questions.q: The most appropriate measure of economic growth is its: [2001]
o: Gross Domestic Product of a country's
questions.e: Per capita real income (NNP at factor cost adjusted for prices) is considered the best measure of economic growth.

questions.q: Match List I (Term) with List II (Explanation): A. Fiscal deficit - B. Budget deficit - C. Revenue deficit - D. Primary deficit. [2000]
questions.e: Fiscal Deficit is Total Expenditure - (Revenue Receipts + Non-debt Capital Receipts). Primary Deficit is Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments.

questions.q: Consider the following taxes: 1️⃣ Corporation tax 2️⃣ Customs duty 3️⃣ Wealth tax 4️⃣ Excise duty. Which of these is/are indirect taxes? [2001]
questions.e: Customs duty and Excise duty are indirect taxes levied on goods, while Corporation and Wealth taxes are direct taxes.

questions.q: The term National Income represents: [2001]
o: gross national product at market prices minus depreciation
gross national product at market prices minus net factor income from abroad
gross national product at market prices minus depreciation and indirect taxes plus subsidies
gross national product at market prices minus depreciation plus net factor income from abroad
questions.e: National Income is Net National Product at factor cost, which is NNP at market prices minus indirect taxes plus subsidies.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Ceiling on foreign exchange for a host of current account transaction heads was lowered in the year 2000. Reason (R): There was a fall in foreign currency assets also. [2001]
o: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are individually true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.e: While the assertion regarding the ceiling is true, the reason relating to a fall in foreign currency assets is false.

questions.q: The prices at which the government purchases food grains for maintaining the public distribution system and for building up buffer-stock is known as: [2001]
questions.e: Procurement price is the price at which the government buys food grains to maintain the PDS and buffer stocks.

questions.q: With reference to Power Sector in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Rural electrification has been treated as a Basic Minimum Service under the Prime Minister's Gramodaya Yojana 2️⃣ 100 percent Foreign Direct Investment in power is allowed without upper limit 3️⃣ The Union Ministry of Power has signed a Memoranda of Understanding with 14 States. [2002]
questions.e: Under PMGY, rural electrification is a basic service. 100% FDI is allowed in power generation, transmission, and distribution.

questions.q: With reference to the Indian Public Finance, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ External liabilities reported in the Union Budget are based on historical exchange rates 2️⃣ The continued high borrowing has kept the real interest rates high in the economy 3️⃣ The upward trend in the ratio of Fiscal Deficit of GDP a recent years has an adverse effect on private investment 4️⃣ Interest payments is the single largest component of the non-plan revenue expenditure of the Union Government. [2002]
questions.e: Statements 2, 3, and 4 correctly describe aspects of Indian public finance; statement 1 is often debated based on budget reporting styles but the sources emphasize the impact of deficits.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Full convertibility of the rupee may mean: 1️⃣ Its free float with the international currencies 2️⃣ Its direct exchange with any other international currency at any prescribed place inside and outside the country 3️⃣ It acts just like any other international currency. [2002]
questions.e: Full convertibility implies the rupee is freely exchangeable for any currency and can be used for cross-border capital flows like any hard currency.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: In India, stamp duties on financial transactions are: 1️⃣ levied and collected by the State Government 2️⃣ appropriated by the Union Government. [2003]
questions.e: Stamp duties are levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States.

questions.q: Which one among the following States has the highest female literacy rate as per the Census 2001? [2003]
questions.e: As per 2001 census among the choices: Chhattisgarh (51.85%), Orissa (50.51%), Madhya Pradesh (50.29%), and Rajasthan (43.85%).

questions.q: Which of the following is not a recommendation of the task force on direct taxes under the chairmanship of Dr. Vijay L. Kelkar in the year 2002? [2004]
o: Exemption from tax on dividends and capital gains from the listed equity
Increase in the exemption limit of personal income to Rs. 1.20 lakh for widows
questions.e: The Kelkar task force actually recommended an exemption limit of Rs 1.50 lakh for widows and senior citizens, not 1.20 lakh.

questions.q: As per 1991 Census, which one of the following groups of Union Territories had the highest literacy rate? [2004]
questions.e: In the 1991 census, Pondicherry (75.3%) and Delhi (74.7%) had the highest literacy rates among UTs.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: As per 2001 Census 1️⃣ the two States with the lowest sex ratio are Haryana and Punjab 2️⃣ the two States with the lowest population per sq. km. of area are Meghalaya and Mizoram 3️⃣ Kerala has both the highest literacy rate and sex ratio. [2004]
questions.e: Statement 1 is wrong because Haryana and Sikkim had the lowest sex ratios. Statement 2 is wrong because Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram had the lowest density. Only statement 3 is correct.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Poverty Reduction and Growth Facility (PRGF) has been established by the International Development Association (IDA) to provide further assistance to low income countries facing high level of indebtedness. 2️⃣ Singapore regional Training Institute (STI) is one of the institutes that provides training in macroeconomic analysis and policy and related subject as a part of programme of the IMF institute. [2005]
questions.e: PRGF was established by the IMF, not the IDA, in 1999 to support poverty reduction in poor member countries.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct? Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBMA) concerns: [2006]
o: Neither fiscal deficit nor revenue deficit
Both fiscal deficit and revenue deficit
questions.e: FRBMA aims to reduce the Fiscal Deficit to 3% and the Revenue Deficit to zero.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct sequence in the decreasing order of contribution of different sectors to the Gross Domestic Product of India? [2007]
questions.e: The contribution sequence is: Services (~55.1%), Industry (~26.4%), and Agriculture (~18.5%).

questions.q: Participatory Notes (PNs) are associated with which one of the following? [2007]
questions.e: PNs are derivative instruments used by foreign investors not registered with SEBI to invest in Indian securities via registered FIIs.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs about India's economic indicator and agricultural production are correctly matched? 1️⃣ GDP per capita (current prices): 37,000 2️⃣ Rice: 180 million tons 3️⃣ Wheat: 75 million tons. [2008]
questions.e: Rice production in 2007-08 was 96.69 million tonnes, making statement 2 incorrect.

questions.q: Consider the following statements with reference to Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS): 1️⃣ All persons of 60 years or above belonging to the households below poverty line in rural areas are eligible. 2️⃣ The Central Assistance under this Scheme is at the rate of 300 per month per beneficiary. [2008]
questions.e: IGNOAPS provides social protection to BPL persons aged 60+; central assistance rates vary, but the eligibility age in the provided context is correct.

questions.q: Consider the following: 1️⃣ Fringe Benefit Tax 2️⃣ Interest Tax 3️⃣ Securities Transaction Tax. Which of the above is/are Direct Tax/Taxes? [2009]
questions.e: FBT (abolished in 2009), STT, and Interest Tax are all categories of direct taxes.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is an appropriate description of deflation? [2010]
o: It is a persistent fall in the general price level of goods and services
It is a fall in the rate of inflation over a period of time
It is a sudden fall in the value of a currency against other currencies
It is a persistent recession in both the financial and real sectors of economy
questions.e: Deflation is a persistent decrease in the general prices of goods and services, occurring when inflation falls below 0%.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are treated as artificial currency? [2010]
questions.e: SDR (Special Drawing Rights) is an artificial currency/reserve asset created by the IMF.

questions.q: When the Reserve Bank of India announces an increase of the Cash Reserve Rate, what does it mean? [2010]
o: The Union Government will have less money to lend
The Reserve Bank of India will have less money to lend
The commercial banks will have less money to lend
The commercial banks will have more money to lend
questions.e: An increase in CRR means banks must keep a larger portion of their deposits with the RBI, leaving them with less liquidity for lending.

questions.q: With reference to India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) in India is available on a monthly basis only. 2️⃣ As compared to Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPIIW), the WPI gives less weight to food articles. [2010]
questions.e: WPI gives less weight to food compared to CPI. While headline WPI is monthly, some components were historically released weekly.

questions.q: In the context of Indian economy, consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Melt down: Fall in stock prices 2️⃣ Recession: Fall in growth rate 3️⃣ Slow down: Fall in GDP. [2010]
questions.e: Recession is technically a fall in GDP (negative growth) for two successive quarters. Slowdown is a fall in the growth rate. Melt down is a rapid fall in asset prices.

questions.q: In the context of governance, consider the following: 1️⃣ Encouraging Foreign Direct Investment inflows 2️⃣ Privatization of higher educational Institutions 3️⃣ Down-sizing of bureaucracy 4️⃣ Selling/offloading the shares of Public Sector Undertakings. Which of the above can be used as measures to control the fiscal deficit in India? [2010]
questions.e: Downsizing bureaucracy (reducing expenditure) and selling PSU shares (disinvestment revenue) are direct measures to control fiscal deficit.

questions.q: With reference to Indian economy, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) has increased by four times in the last 10 years. 2️⃣ The percentage share of Public Sector in GDP has declined in the last 10 years. [2010]
questions.e: While GDP grew, it did not increase fourfold in that specific 10-year window; however, the public sector's share in the economy has consistently declined.

questions.q: India is regarded as a country with "Demographic Dividend". This is due to [2011-1]
o: Its high population in the age group of 15-64 years.
Its high population in the age group below 15 years.
Its high population in the age group above 65 years.
questions.e: Demographic dividend refers to the economic growth potential resulting from a rising share of the working-age population (15-64 years).

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a feature of "Value Added Tax"? [2011-1]
o: It is basically a subject of the central government and the state governments are only a facilitator for its successful implementation.
It is multi-point destination-based system of taxation.
It is a tax levied on value addition at each stage of transaction in the production distribution chain.
It is a tax on the final consumption of goods or services and must ultimately be borne by the consumer.
questions.e: VAT on the sale/purchase of goods is a State subject (Entry 54, State List); the Central Government only acts as a facilitator.

questions.q: Karl Marx explained the process of class struggle with the help of which one of the following theories? [2011-1]
questions.e: Marx used Dialectical Materialism to explain that all development is a result of the struggle or conflict of opposites.

questions.q: All revenues received by the Union Government by way of taxes and other receipts for the conduct of Government business are credited to the? [2011-1]
questions.e: Under Article 266(1), all tax and non-tax revenues, loans, and repayments are credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.q: A rapid increase in the rate of inflation is sometimes attributed to the "base effect". What is "base effect"? [2011-1]
o: None of the statements (a), (b) and (c) given above is correct in this context
It is the impact of the price levels of previous year on the calculation of inflation rate
It is the impact of the surge in demand due to rapid economic growth
It is the impact of drastic deficiency in supply due to failure of crops
questions.e: The base effect refers to the impact of the price level of the corresponding period in the previous year on the current inflation calculation.

questions.q: In the context of Indian economy, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The growth rate of GDP has steadily increased in the last five years. 2️⃣ The growth rate in per capita income has steadily increased in the last five years. [2011-1]
questions.e: Growth rates fluctuated during the mid-to-late 2000s, especially due to the 2008 global recession, so they did not increase "steadily".

questions.q: In India, which of the following have the highest share in the disbursement of credit to agriculture and allied activities? [2011-1]
questions.e: Commercial banks account for approximately 60% of credit disbursement to agriculture, followed by Cooperative banks (30%) and RRBs.

questions.q: Which of the following are the methods of Parliamentary control over public finance in India? 1️⃣ Placing Annual Financial Statement before the Parliament 2️⃣ Withdrawal of moneys from Consolidated Fund of India only after passing the Appropriation Bill 3️⃣ Provisions of supplementary grants and vote-on-account 4️⃣ A periodic or at least a mid-year review of programme of the Government against macroeconomic forecasts and expenditure by a Parliamentary Budget Office 5️⃣ Introducing Finance Bill in the Parliament. [2012-1]
questions.e: The Parliament controls finance through the Annual Financial Statement, Appropriation Bills, Supplementary grants, and the Finance Bill. A Parliamentary Budget Office is not a standard feature in India.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) acts as a bankers' bank. This would imply which of the following? 1️⃣ Other banks retain their deposits with the RBI. 2️⃣ The RBI lends funds to the commercial banks in times of need. 3️⃣ The RBI advises the commercial banks on monetary matters. [2012-1]
questions.e: As a bankers' bank, RBI holds bank deposits (CRR), provides liquidity (lender of last resort), and gives guidance on monetary policy.

questions.q: In India, deficit financing is used for raising resources for [2013-1]
questions.e: Deficit financing—spending more than earning—is used in India to provide the necessary impetus for economic development.

questions.q: Priority Sector Lending by banks in India constitutes the lending to [2013-1]
questions.e: Priority sector lending includes agriculture, MSMEs, education, housing, and weaker sections.

questions.q: Which one of the following groups of items is included in India's foreign-exchange reserves? [2013-1]
o: Foreign-currency assets, gold holdings of the RBI and SDR's
Foreign-currency assets, gold holdings of the RBI and loans from the World Bank
Foreign-currency assets, loans from the World Bank and SDRs
Foreign-currency assets, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) and loans from foreign countries
questions.e: India's forex reserves consist of foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs, and the IMF reserve position.

questions.q: The national income of a country for a given period is equal to the [2013-1]
o: sum of personal income of all individuals
money value of final goods and services produced
total value of goods and services produced by the nationals
sum of total consumption and investment expenditure
questions.e: National Income is defined as the money value of all final goods and services produced within an economy in a year.

questions.q: Which of the following constitute Capital Account? 1️⃣ Foreign Loans 2️⃣ Foreign Direct Investment 3️⃣ Private Remittances 4️⃣ Portfolio Investment. [2013-1]
questions.e: Capital account includes foreign loans, FDI, and portfolio investment. Private remittances belong to the Current Account.

questions.q: In the context of Indian economy, 'Open Market Operations' refers to [2013-1]
o: lending by commercial banks to industry and trade
borrowing by scheduled banks from the RBI
purchase and sale of government securities by the RBI
questions.e: Open Market Operations (OMO) involve the RBI buying or selling government securities to regulate money supply.

questions.q: The main objective of the 12th Five-Year Plan is [2014-1]
o: faster, sustainable and more inclusive growth
sustainable and inclusive growth to reduce unemployment
questions.e: The 12th Plan (2012-17) aimed for faster, sustainable, and more inclusive growth.

questions.q: The terms 'Marginal Standing Facility Rate' and 'Net Demand and Time Liabilities', sometimes appearing in news, are used in relation to [2014-1]
o: supply and demand of agricultural products
questions.e: MSF is a rate for overnight borrowing from RBI, and NDTL is used to calculate bank liabilities; both are banking terms.

questions.q: With reference to Indian economy, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The rate of growth of Real Gross Domestic Product has steadily increased in the last decade. 2️⃣ The Gross Domestic Product at market prices (in rupees) has steadily increased in the last decade. [2015-1]
questions.e: While the growth rate fluctuated (dipping after the 2008 recession), the absolute GDP at market prices has increased every year for the last decade.

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes the term "Merchant Discount Rate" sometimes seen in news? [2018-1]
o: The amount paid back by banks to their customers when they use debit cards for financial transactions for purchasing goods or services.
The incentive given by the Government, to merchants for promoting digital payments by their customers through Point of Sale (PoS) machines and debit cards.
The charge to a merchant by a bank for accepting payments from his customers through the bank's debit cards.
The incentive given by a bank to a merchant for accepting payments through debit cards pertaining to that bank.
questions.e: MDR is the fee a merchant pays to a bank for the privilege of accepting payments via debit or credit cards.

questions.q: With reference to digital payments, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ BHIM app allows the user to transfer money to anyone with a UPI-enabled bank account. 2️⃣ While a chip-pin debit card has four factors of authentication, BHIM app has only two factors of authentication. [2018-1]
questions.e: BHIM has three levels of authentication (Device ID/Mobile number, Bank Account sync, and User-created PIN).

questions.q: Which one of the following links all the ATMs in India? [2018-1]
questions.e: The NPCI operates the National Financial Switch (NFS), which provides the linkage for the ATM network in India.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) is the amount that banks have to maintain in the form of their own funds to offset any loss that banks incur if the account-holders fail to repay dues. 2️⃣ CAR is decided by each individual bank. [2018-1]
questions.e: CAR is not decided by individual banks; it is determined by benchmarks set by the Basel Committee and implemented by the central bank (RBI).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Review Committee Report has recommended a debt to GDP ratio of 60% for the general (combined) government by 2023, comprising 40% for the Central Government and 20% for the State Governments. 2️⃣ The Central Government has domestic liabilities of 21% of GDP as compared to that of 49% of GDP of the State Governments. 3️⃣ As per the Constitution of India, it is mandatory for a State to take the Central Government's consent for raising any loan if the former owes any outstanding liabilities to the latter. [2018-1]
questions.e: Statement 2 is incorrect as the Central Government's domestic liability is approximately 46%, not 21%. Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

questions.q: Consider the following items: 1️⃣ Cereal grains hulted 2️⃣ Chicken eggs cooked 3️⃣ Fish processed and canned 4️⃣ Newspaper containing advertising material. Which of the above items is/are exempted under GST (Goods and Services Tax)? [2018-1]
questions.e: Processed/canned food is subject to GST, whereas newspapers (sold to public) and basic items like hulled cereals/eggs are generally exempted.

questions.q: With reference to India's decision to levy an equalization tax of 6% on online advertisement services offered by non-resident entities, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ It is introduced as a part of the Income Tax Act. 2️⃣ Non-resident entities that offer advertisement services in India can claim a tax credit in their home country under the "Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements". [2018-1]
questions.e: Equalization levy was introduced as a separate legislation under the Finance Bill (2016), and it does not allow for tax credits under DTAA.

questions.q: Despite being a high saving economy, capital formation may not result in significant increase in output due to [2018-1]
questions.e: A high capital-output ratio means more capital is needed to produce one unit of output, slowing down the impact of capital formation on growth.

questions.q: Which of the following is not included in the assets of a commercial bank in India? [2019-1]
o: Money at call and short notice
questions.e: Deposits are liabilities for a bank because they must be repaid to the customers; advances and investments are assets.

questions.q: In the context of India, which of the following factors is/are contributor/contributors to reducing the risk of a currency crisis? 1️⃣ The foreign currency earnings of India's IT sector. 2️⃣ Increasing the government expenditure. 3️⃣ Remittances from Indians abroad. [2019-1]
questions.e: Inflows of dollars (via IT earnings and remittances) reduce the risk of a currency crisis. Increasing government expenditure can backfire by causing inflation.

questions.q: The Chairman of public sector banks are selected by the [2019-1]
questions.e: The Banks Board Bureau (BBB), set up in 2016, selects top officials (MD, CEO, Chairman) for Public Sector Banks.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) is the first regulatory body set up by the Government of India. 2️⃣ One of the tasks of PNGRB is to ensure competitive markets for gas. 3️⃣ Appeals against the decisions of PNGRB go before the Appellate Tribunals of Electricity. [2019-1]
questions.e: PNGRB was set up in 2006; many other bodies like SEBI (1988) existed earlier. Its tasks include ensuring gas market competition and appeals go to APTEL.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India's recent directives relating to 'Storage of Payment System Data', popularly known as data diktat command the payment system providers that : 1️⃣ They shall ensure that entire data relating to payment systems operated by them are stored in a system only in India. 2️⃣ They shall ensure that the systems are owned and operated by public sector enterprises. 3️⃣ They shall submit the consolidated system audit report to the comptroller and Auditor General of India by the end of the calendar year. [2019-1]
questions.e: RBI's directive specifically mandates that payment system data must be stored only in India. The other requirements listed are not part of the directive.

questions.q: What is the importance of the term "Interest Coverage Ratio" of a firm in India? 1️⃣ It helps in understanding the present risk of a firm that a bank is going to give a loan to. 2️⃣ It helps in evaluating the emerging risk of a firm that a bank is going to give a loan to. 3️⃣ The higher a borrowing firm's level of Interest Coverage Ratio, the worse is its ability to service its debt. [2020-1]
questions.e: A higher interest coverage ratio actually means a firm is better able to service its debt; thus, statement 3 is incorrect.

questions.q: With reference to the following statements: 1️⃣ 'Commercial Paper is a short-term unsecured promissory note. 2️⃣ 'Certificate of Deposit is a long-term instrument issued by the Reserve Bank of India to a corporation. 3️⃣ 'Call Money' is a short-term finance used for interbank transactions. 4️⃣ 'Zero-Coupon Bonds' are the interest bearing short-term bonds issued by the Scheduled Commercial Banks to corporations. [2020-1]
questions.e: Certificates of Deposit are short-term instruments. Zero-coupon bonds are issued at a discount and do not bear regular interest. Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

questions.q: In the context of the Indian economy, non-financial debt includes which of the following? 1️⃣ Housing loans owed by households 2️⃣ Amounts outstanding on credit cards 3️⃣ Treasury bills. [2020-1]
questions.e: Non-financial debt excludes debt from financial institutions that borrow solely to re-lend. Loans for consumption or government bills qualify as non-financial debt.
